theme: A freelance designer: clients, rates, tools
facts: My day rate for design work is 900 dollars, and hourly work is 120.
Rush jobs get a 30 percent surcharge on top of the quoted price.

Fernhill Outfitters pays slowly and always asks for a discount. Lou, their brand manager, wants three concepts instead of one. I quote them a 10 percent buffer on top of the usual rate so I have room to negotiate. Their invoices go to the accounts mailbox, not to Lou directly.
Bluebird Studio's contract for the logo refresh was signed on June 3rd.

Northwind Coffee's invoices are usually paid within a week, so they get priority scheduling when a rush comes up. Their owner, Alex, prefers short calls and a single shared document. Revisions for Northwind are capped at two rounds because they tend to change direction late.

Quotes are valid for fourteen days and must list what is included and what is excluded. Any change requested after sign-off counts as a new quote, even if it seems small. I do not agree to unpaid revisions in writing. Quotes are sent as PDFs so that clients cannot edit the numbers.
Final design files are delivered in layered PDF and PNG formats, plus the source file.
I take client work Monday to Thursday and keep one day a week for myself.

Invoices are sent at the start and at the milestone, with half up front. The final payment is due before the source files are handed over. Late payments get a reminder on day three and a second notice after seven days. Work stops if a client is more than thirty days late.
My main design tool is a vector app, with templates kept in the team folder.
I use a notes app for client notes and keep one page per client.

Moodboards are shared only after the brief is signed, and they are never reused for another client. Each project gets a folder with brief, references, drafts, and final files. References from competitors are noted but not copied. I keep a short retro after every project in the same notes app.
Mina Cho is the art director at Bluebird Studio and approves the final colors.
I charge a flat fee for logos, since research is included.
I don't take on new clients between the first and the tenth of any month.

Clients who want a full brand identity get a discount on the second phase if the first phase is paid within two weeks. Phase two includes stationery and a basic website template. I do not offer discounts on phase one. Any extra work beyond the template goes into a separate quote.
My portfolio site is updated after every completed project, with client permission.
I keep a spreadsheet of all invoices, and it's reviewed every quarter with my accountant.
Clients get a weekly progress update by email, sent at the end of the week.

When a client asks for feedback, I expect answers within three business days. If they do not respond after a reminder, the project pauses and the deadline shifts by the same number of days. I say this clearly in the contract. Feedback should be given in one consolidated message, not scattered across chats.
I only accept clients referred by people I know, or via my inbound form.
My accountant is Ellen Park, and she files taxes in April.
I'm reachable by phone on weekdays only, between 9 and 11 a.m.

A non-disclosure agreement is required before I see any unreleased product plan from a client. The NDA is signed on the first call. Sharing a client's name, product, or sketches with another person without permission breaks the agreement. I keep a short list of NDAs in the notes app.
